summary: Our project, Earth Trend Detective, developed by Women Beyond Earth, is an interactive tool designed to help people understand how environmental conditions change over time using NASA data and statistical methods. It allows users to explore different environmental variables and locations, identify trends, and better understand issues such as Arctic warming and climate change in their local communities. By transforming scientific data into accessible visualizations and understandable information, our project addresses the challenge of making Earth system trends easier for everyone to investigate. We believe environmental awareness is essential to recognizing the causes and impacts of climate change and inspiring meaningful action. Our goal is to promote climate education, encourage sustainable choices, and strengthen collective responsibility for protecting our planet. Moving forward, we hope to make the tool more mobile-friendly and expand its data and interactive features to make environmental knowledge accessible to everyone, anywhere.
details:
Earth Trend Detective is an interactive website developed by Women Beyond Earth to make environmental data easier to explore, understand, and interpret. The platform uses NASA POWER API to access environmental data and applies statistical methods to investigate how environmental conditions change over time across different locations. Specifically, it incorporates the Mann-Kendall test, a statistical method used to identify significant trends in environmental data, and Sen's Slope, which estimates the rate of change over time. Together, these methods help users understand whether environmental conditions are increasing or decreasing and how quickly they are changing.

Users can select environmental variables, locations, and data series to visualize trends through interactive graphs and explore statistical results, including the direction and rate of change, as well as the total change over the selected period. For example, users can investigate Arctic warming and examine how air temperatures have changed over the years.

Our project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Leaflet supporting interactive mapping features. By combining these technologies with NASA's environmental data and statistical analysis, we created an educational tool that transforms complex scientific information into accessible visual representations.

One of the main benefits of our project is that it allows people, including those without a scientific background, to better understand environmental changes. Its intended impact is to strengthen environmental awareness, promote climate education, and encourage individuals to make more sustainable decisions.

What makes our project creative is its combination of real scientific data, statistical analysis, and interactive exploration. Rather than simply presenting environmental facts, we encourage users to investigate trends themselves and connect global environmental changes with their local communities. Throughout development, we considered accessibility, clarity, ease of use, and the importance of making scientific information understandable to different audiences.

Our future plans include improving mobile accessibility and expanding the website's data and interactive features so that environmental knowledge becomes accessible to everyone, anywhere.
